  1. Storage URIs

Storage URIs

storageUri in models and model.uri in llmInferenceServices accept several schemes. The storage initializer downloads the artifact and mounts it at /mnt/models.

Supported schemes

Scheme Example Credentials
hf:// hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct HF_TOKEN for gated or private repositories
s3:// s3://bucket/models/fraud/v3 Secret annotated for S3, attached to the ServiceAccount
gs:// gs://bucket/models/fraud/v3 Google service account key or Workload Identity
https:// https://example.com/model.joblib None, or a public URL
pvc:// pvc://model-store/fraud/v3 None; the PVC must exist in the workload namespace
oci:// oci://registry.example.com/models/fraud:v3 Image pull secret

Hugging Face

See Hugging Face for tokens, gated repositories, and mirrors.

models:
  - name: embeddings
    runtime: kserve-huggingfaceserver
    modelFormat: huggingface
    storageUri: hf://sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2

S3 and S3-compatible storage

Create a Secret with the storage annotation, then attach it to the ServiceAccount used by the predictor.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: s3-credentials
  namespace: models
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/s3-endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com
    serving.kserve.io/s3-usehttps: "1"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-region: eu-west-1
type: Opaque
stringData:
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: "replace-me"
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: "replace-me"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: s3-sa
  namespace: models
secrets:
  - name: s3-credentials

Reference that ServiceAccount:

models:
  - name: fraud-detector
    runtime: kserve-sklearnserver
    modelFormat: sklearn
    storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3
    serviceAccountName: s3-sa

Setting serviceAccountName replaces the chart’s hf-sa. If the same workload also needs Hugging Face access, attach both Secrets to that one ServiceAccount.

MinIO and other S3-compatible systems use the same annotations:

  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/s3-endpoint: minio.storage.svc.cluster.local:9000
    serving.kserve.io/s3-usehttps: "0"

Cluster-wide S3 defaults can be set once:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    storage:
      s3:
        endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com
        region: eu-west-1
        useHttps: "1"

Google Cloud Storage 

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: gcs-credentials
  namespace: models
type: Opaque
stringData:
  gcloud-application-credentials.json: |
    {"type": "service_account", "project_id": "replace-me"}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: gcs-sa
  namespace: models
secrets:
  - name: gcs-credentials

models:
  - name: demand-forecast
    runtime: kserve-xgbserver
    modelFormat: xgboost
    storageUri: gs://models/demand/v7
    serviceAccountName: gcs-sa

Persistent volume claims

Best for large models reused by many workloads and for air-gapped clusters.

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: model-store
  namespace: models
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadOnlyMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 500Gi

models:
  - name: cached-llm
    runtime: kserve-vllmserver
    modelFormat: huggingface
    storageUri: pvc://model-store/llama-3.1-8b

The path after the claim name is the directory inside the volume. Use ReadWriteMany or ReadOnlyMany so several pods can mount it.

Populate the volume with a one-off job:

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: seed-model-store
  namespace: models
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: seed
          image: python:3.11-slim
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
          args:
            - |
              pip install --no-cache-dir huggingface_hub
              python -c "
              from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
              snapshot_download('meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct',
                                local_dir='/mnt/store/llama-3.1-8b')
              "
          env:
            - name: HF_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: hf-secret
                  key: HF_TOKEN
          volumeMounts:
            - name: store
              mountPath: /mnt/store
      volumes:
        - name: store
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: model-store

OCI registries

Models packaged as OCI artifacts, sometimes called modelcars.

models:
  - name: packaged-model
    runtime: kserve-sklearnserver
    modelFormat: sklearn
    storageUri: oci://registry.example.com/models/fraud:v3

Modelcar behavior is configured upstream:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    storage:
      enableModelcar: true
      uidModelcar: 1010

Private registries need an image pull secret on the ServiceAccount:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: oci-sa
  namespace: models
imagePullSecrets:
  - name: registry-credentials

HTTPS

Single-file artifacts served over HTTP or HTTPS:

models:
  - name: simple-model
    runtime: kserve-sklearnserver
    modelFormat: sklearn
    storageUri: https://models.example.com/fraud/v3/model.joblib

Custom certificate authorities:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    storage:
      caBundleConfigMapName: custom-ca-bundle
      caBundleVolumeMountPath: /etc/ssl/custom-certs

Choosing a scheme 

flowchart TD
    A[Where is the model?] --> B{Public Hugging Face model?}
    B -- Yes --> C[hf://]
    B -- No --> D{Cluster has internet?}
    D -- No --> E[pvc:// or s3:// mirror]
    D -- Yes --> F{Already in object storage?}
    F -- Yes --> G[s3:// or gs://]
    F -- No --> H{Reused by many pods?}
    H -- Yes --> I[pvc://]
    H -- No --> J[oci:// or https://]
